transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I came in because when I start eating, it feels like I kind of disappear and something else takes over. Even when I’m telling myself to stop, I just keep going until I can’t stand it anymore.
During those times, do you eat an unusually large amount of food?

Yeah. There are nights after studying where I’ll eat dinner at the dining hall, then go back to my room and keep eating—burgers, cereal, peanut butter, snacks, whatever I can find. It’s way more than a normal dinner, until the trash is full and I feel sick.
After you eat that way, do you ever make yourself vomit?

Yeah. Usually afterward I’ll find a bathroom in the dorm, or sometimes a quiet floor in the library, and make myself throw up. I’m just terrified that all the food is sitting there and turning into weight.
Are you currently at a significantly low body weight for your height?
I’m not really sure what counts as significantly low. I don’t think I look unusually thin, but I haven’t really checked my weight against my height.
Are you very afraid of gaining weight?

Yeah, I am. If I catch my reflection and think my stomach or face looks bigger than the other guys, it can ruin my whole day. I feel like I’ve failed at everything, and I just don’t want anyone to look at me.
What is your current height and weight?
I don’t know exactly. I haven’t weighed myself recently, and I’m not sure about my height either—around average, I think.
Besides making yourself vomit, do you ever use laxatives, diuretics, or other methods to try to get rid of the calories after eating?
I’m not sure what you mean by other methods. I don’t really know much about laxatives or diuretics.
After you eat like that, do you ever go without eating for a long time to try to make up for it?
I’m not really sure. What do you mean by going without eating for a long time?
After you binge eat, do you ever intentionally not eat for a whole day or most of a day to make up for it?
I’m not sure. I mean, I don’t really keep track of it like that.
Has anyone recently told you that you are underweight?
No, nobody’s said that to me recently.
Do your clothes fit loosely because you’ve lost a lot of weight?
I haven’t really noticed my clothes fitting looser, no.
After you binge eat, do you ever exercise hard on purpose to try to undo the calories?
I’m not really sure what counts as exercising hard. I don’t think I’ve thought of it as trying to undo calories.
Do you think you are underweight right now?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think of myself as underweight.
After a binge, do you ever deliberately skip all food for the next day to make up for it?
I’m not sure I’ve done that exactly—like skipped all food the whole next day.
What was your most recent weight?
I don’t know exactly. I haven’t checked my weight recently.
Have you been told your weight by a doctor or nurse anytime in the past year?
I don’t think so. Not that I can remember.
Has a doctor or nurse ever told you that you were underweight?
I don’t think anyone’s ever told me that, no.
Do you know your pants waist size?
I’m not really sure. I don’t pay much attention to the waist size on my pants.
How often do you make yourself throw up after eating that way?
Usually after I eat like that. I’ll go to a bathroom in the dorm or somewhere quiet in the library and make myself throw up because I’m scared it’s just turning into weight.
How often do these binge-and-vomit episodes happen?
Several times a week, for most of this semester. It’s been going on for at least the last few months—I can’t really think of a week where it just stopped.
